_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head-term for the generic fancy-text generator job; already the H1/title of the flagship NL page. Use as the default umbrella term when no more specific style is meant.
phrases.good_example: Gratis lettertype generator: mooie letters, sierletters, aesthetic fonts en coole symbolen om te kopiëren en plakken.
phrases.avoid_when: when the specific style being discussed is bold, script, or gothic — use the more specific term instead

phrases.usage_guidance: Correct, natural Dutch term for calligraphic/script-style Unicode letters. On the homepage FAQ this is explicitly distinguished from 'schuine letters (cursief/italic)' — keep that separation intact when writing copy that discusses both. || REVISED 2026-07-26: lead with the CLOSED COMPOUND 'sierletters', not the adjectival 'sierlijke letters' -- GSC shows the compound outperforming the adjectival ~3:1 on impressions (441 vs 145). Keep both in the title; the compound goes first. The sierletters/schuine-letters disambiguation above still stands.
phrases.good_example: Sierletters voor namen en quotes (𝓁𝒾𝑒𝓋𝑒 𝓋𝒾𝒷𝑒𝓈)
phrases.avoid_when: when italic/slanted text (not script/calligraphic) is meant — use 'schuine letters' instead

phrases.usage_guidance: In standard Dutch, 'cursief' is the everyday and typographically correct word for italic (slanted) text — it is NOT the natural Dutch word for flowing calligraphic/script handwriting style. The site's own homepage FAQ and Discord formatting guide both use it this way correctly ('Wat is het verschil met gewoon vet of cursief typen?'; Discord markdown '*cursief*' -> real italic). Use 'cursief' when the real italic slant (native formatting or the italic-fonts Unicode set) is meant.
phrases.avoid_when: do not use 'cursief' as the label for the script/handwriting-style Unicode font family — see NL-004 for the site's own internal conflict on this point

phrases.usage_guidance: Used interchangeably with 'cursief' on the homepage ('schuine letters (cursief / italic)') and independently ('schuine sierletters', 'schuine fonts'). Natural, safe synonym for italic; also combines with sierletters to describe the aesthetic-tilted script look used in TikTok captions.
phrases.good_example: Voor captions worden vooral schuine sierletters en kleine hoofdletters (sᴍᴀʟʟ ᴄᴀᴘs) gebruikt

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary, natural umbrella term for symbols/glyphs; matches the dedicated library hub. See NL-020 'vreemde tekens' for a natural near-synonym used more in a troubleshooting/rendering-failure context.
phrases.good_example: Waarom zie ik soms een vierkantje (□) in plaats van een teken?

phrases.english_concept: boxes/squares shown instead of a glyph (tofu rendering failure)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is one of the most heavily reused FAQ answers on the whole NL site — near-identical 'vierkantje (□) betekent dat het toestel... niet kent' phrasing appears on at least 8 different pages. It is the correct, natural Dutch term for this failure mode and should keep being reused verbatim/near-verbatim for consistency. 'Blokjes' is used as a casual synonym in the same sentence on nl/mooie-letters/.
phrases.good_example: Een vierkantje (□) betekent dat het toestel van de lezer dat specifieke teken niet kent — vaak een ouder toestel of een verouderde app.

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary, natural, already-live term for this feature; the dedicated page also naturally uses 'lege spatie', 'blokje' (for a failed/rejected invisible char) and 'schijnbaar leeg WhatsApp-bericht'.
phrases.good_example: Kopieer een onzichtbaar teken en plak het in de Instagram-bio voor lege regels of nette witruimte, of stuur het als een schijnbaar leeg WhatsApp-bericht.

phrases.usage_guidance: This distinction matters functionally: Unicode styling works in the weergavenaam but is stripped from the strict a-z/0-9 @gebruikersnaam handle. The Discord guide gets this exactly right and should be the model for any other platform page that needs to explain the same username-vs-display-name split.
phrases.good_example: De @gebruikersnaam weigert het. [...] Style in plaats daarvan je weergavenaam.

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard Dutch word for a server-level nickname (as opposed to weergavenaam/gebruikersnaam, see NL-009). Also the standard word used site-wide in Dutch tech press for changing a Discord nickname.
Primary, natural, already-live term for the bold category page.

Standard, correct, everyday Dutch verb pair — used consistently site-wide and by every Dutch competitor tool. No natural slang alternative needed; do not substitute 'knippen en plakken' (cut and paste), which is a different action.
phrases.good_example: Druk op kopiëren, plak het in je bio, caption of WhatsApp, klaar.
phrases.avoid_when: do not confuse with 'knippen en plakken' (cut and paste)

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural, standard term, already live on the bio-font usecase page ('Live preview en tekenlimieten voor Instagram, TikTok, Discord...'). Confirmed as the term Dutch character-counter tools also use as their own brand name (tekenstellen.nl).
phrases.good_example: Live preview en tekenlimieten voor Instagram, TikTok, Discord, X, WhatsApp, Facebook & Tinder

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural, direct translation, used correctly alongside 'stoer/edgy' register on the homepage's gaming-names FAQ answer.
phrases.good_example: Gotische letters (𝔡𝔞𝔯𝔨𝔚𝔬𝔩𝔣), zalgo voor horror-vibes, doorgestreepte tekst voor een 'glitched' look.

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural direct translation, already live as a dedicated page title; the borrowed English term 'small caps' is kept parenthetically alongside it site-wide, which matches how the term is actually used by Dutch audiences (both forms circulate).

Kept untranslated on purpose — the homepage FAQ explicitly explains it rather than translating it ('Met "aesthetic letters" bedoelen de meeste mensen die rustige, fijne look...'), which matches how the word is actually used by young Dutch social-media users: as an unglossed English loanword, not calqued into Dutch. Do not force a Dutch translation like 'esthetisch' in this context register — that reads stiff/formal, not native usage.
phrases.good_example: Wat zijn aesthetic letters en hoe krijg ik die look?

phrases.english_concept: strange/odd characters (near-synonym of special characters, skews troubleshooting)
phrases.usage_guidance: Natural near-synonym of 'speciale tekens' (NL-006) but with a troubleshooting/confusion connotation rather than a browse/discovery one — fits an answer-style FAQ ('why do I see vreemde tekens') better than a library hub title. A dedicated Dutch competitor site (vreemdetekens.nl) uses this exact phrase as its brand name, confirming real independent search demand distinct from 'speciale tekens'.
phrases.good_example: Commando om vreemde tekens en symbolen uit woord te halen
phrases.avoid_when: do not use as the primary hub label (that's 'speciale tekens') — this fits FAQ/troubleshooting copy specifically
